extracted.intended_audience: The people of the State of New York (citizens considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the adequacy, safeguards, and principles governing the size, composition, and selection of the House of Representatives under the proposed U.S. Constitution. Focuses on representation ratios, accountability mechanisms, sources of local knowledge, and anti-corruption provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common measure for representation and taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: By extending the rule for apportioning representation to taxation as well, the States will have opposite interests (to swell representation vs. to reduce taxation) which will control and balance each other, producing requisite impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion argues for tying representation and taxation to the same census-based rule so that states have countervailing incentives (to exaggerate population for representation, to underreport for taxation), which limits bias in census returns and improves accuracy of apportionment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of individual votes in federal legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposed Constitution, the federal acts will take effect without the necessary intervention of the individual States; they will depend merely on the majority of votes in the federal legislature, and consequently each vote... will have an equal weight and efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats votes of representatives as equal in weight regardless of the size or wealth of the State they represent, analogous to equal-value votes in state legislatures; implication is that design accepts this equality as a feature, not a defect, and must be judged by its consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate size of a representative assembly (minimum and maximum)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain number at least seems to be necessary to secure the benefits of free consultation and discussion, and to guard against too easy a combination for improper purposes; on the other hand, the number ought at most to be kept within a certain limit, in order to avoid the confusion and intemperance of a multitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether proposed membership levels strike a balance: sufficient members to ensure deliberation and prevent collusion, but not so many as to produce internecine confusion or mob-like passion. Use qualitative judgment, not arithmetic alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of limited powers and biennial elections on required size
rubrics_metrics.description: For the same reason that the limited powers of the Congress, and the control of the State legislatures, justify less frequent elections than the public safely might otherwise require, the members of the Congress need be less numerous than if they possessed the whole power of legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing required representative numbers, consider the scope of federal authority and the frequency of elections: narrower federal powers and state checks permit a smaller representative body without endangering liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of ratio: one representative per thirty thousand inhabitants
rubrics_metrics.description: The number which is to prevail in the first instance... will not exceed one for every thirty thousand inhabitants; estimating growth, such a ratio will raise the number of representatives sufficiently over time to allay fears of smallness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defends the constitution's cap (one per 30,000) as a practicable ceiling and explains that periodic censuses and population growth will increase representation over time; uses comparative and demographic reasoning to justify the ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility of sitting members to newly created or made more lucrative civil offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The members of the Congress are rendered ineligible to any civil offices that may be created, or of which the emoluments may be increased, during the term of their election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constitutional constraint is presented as a safeguard against corruption via appointments: it limits the President's ability to buy loyalty by promising offices to currently sitting representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative needs knowledge only of matters within federal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle that the representative ought to be acquainted with the interests and circumstances of his constituents can extend no further than to those circumstances and interests to which the authority and care of the representative relate... the objects of federal legislation are commerce, taxation, and the militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging the adequacy of representatives' local knowledge, focus on whether they understand matters relevant to federal jurisdiction (commerce regulation, duties/taxes, militia organization) rather than expecting intimate familiarity with all local minutiae.

rubrics_metrics.name: State laws and legislators supply local information to the federal legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws of the State, framed by representatives from every part of it, will be almost of themselves a sufficient guide... The representatives of each State will probably in all cases have been members, and may even at the very time be members, of the State legislature, from whence local information may be conveyed by a very few hands into the legislature of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that federal legislators will benefit from existing state codes and state-legislative experience, reducing the need for large numbers of federal representatives to gather local facts; use state legislative records and personnel as a channel for local expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Larger electorates (thousands) are at least as capable as small electorates (hundreds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it reasonable to maintain that five or six thousand citizens are less capable of choosing a fit representative, or more liable to be corrupted by an unfit one, than five or six hundred? Reason, on the contrary, assures us, that as in so great a number a fit representative would be most likely to be found, so the choice would be less likely to be diverted by intrigues or bribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defends districts electing representatives by thousands of voters: larger electorates increase the chance of finding qualified candidates and reduce susceptibility to corruption or manipulation compared to very small electorates or restrictive property-based franchises.

rubrics_metrics.name: No property/birth/religious/civil-profession qualifications should restrict eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Not the rich more than the poor; not the learned more than the ignorant; not the haughty heirs of distinguished names more than the humble sons of obscurity and unpropitious fortune. No qualification of wealth, of birth, of religious faith, or of civil profession is permitted to fetter the judgement or disappoint the inclination of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that the elective principle of republican government requires broad eligibility and absence of formal social or property qualifications, so that the people may choose representatives from all classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislators restrained because laws operate equally on them and their constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: They can make no law which will not have its full operation on themselves and their friends, as well as on the great mass of the society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats reciprocity of law application as a practical restraint on self-serving legislation: laws that affect lawmakers as well as the public create alignment of interests between representatives and constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional mechanism for periodic augmentation via decennial census
rubrics_metrics.description: Within every successive period of ten years a census of inhabitants is to be repeated... to readjust from time to time the apportionment of representatives to the number of inhabitants, and to augment the number of representatives at the same periods, under the sole limitation that the whole number shall not exceed one for every thirty thousand inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the procedural safeguard to keep representation proportional over time: decennial censuses and reapportionment rules ensure gradual increases in representatives as population grows, subject to the 1/30,000 cap and at least one representative per State.
